answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The nectar multiplier is published, charged in opal, and vine lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1571 identities would post 2119 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
